skill.name: onboarding-helper
skill.description: Generate developer onboarding guides, setup checklists, learning plans, and team process documentation for new engineers joining a project.
skill.summary: Create structured onboarding material for new developers.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline examples, placeholder environment variables, and reference links in a documentation template. The audit confirms remote installer guidance that tells users to execute downloaded shell scripts, and it adds semantic concerns for credential-handling guidance and a weak sample password. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Remote installer commands are copied into onboarding material.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell and bash command substitution with package-manager instructions that verify checksums or link to official install documentation.

remediation.issue: Credential request wording points users to broad team channels.
remediation.suggestion: Route all credential requests through a ticket or vault workflow, and state that secrets must never be pasted in chat.

remediation.issue: The sample login uses a weak shared password.
remediation.suggestion: Use generated temporary test credentials or account-specific credentials, and mark examples as non-production.
Ask users to identify the process first, then stop only the intended local service.

static_findings.snippet: - **Port 3000 in use**: Kill the process with `lsof -ti:3000 | xargs kill -9`
- **Database connection failed**: Check Docker is running with `docker ps`
- **Module not found**: Delete `node_modules` and run `npm install` again
**Finding Tasks**: Check Jira board for issues labeled `good-first-issue`.
- **Port 3000 in use**: Kill the process with `lsof -ti:3000 | xargs kill -9`
Check 1Password vault "Development Secrets" or ask in #engineering.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Request Guidance Uses Broad Team Channels
semantic_findings.description: The template tells users to request AWS credentials from DevOps in the engineering channel and to ask there for API credentials. This can lead to secret disclosure unless all sharing stays inside an approved vault workflow.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines connect credential requests with a broad engineering channel. They do not explicitly tell users to paste secrets, so confidence is high-medium rather than very high.

semantic_findings.title: Weak Shared Test Password in Template
semantic_findings.description: The guide lists a reusable test login with the password password123. New-hire documentation should avoid weak shared passwords, even for sample accounts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The weak password is explicit in the onboarding template. It appears to be test-only, so the likely impact is limited.

content.value_statement: Developer onboarding often scatters setup steps, team norms, and first tasks across many places. This skill creates structured onboarding guides with timelines, checklists, resources, and starter tasks.
actual_capabilities: Drafts full developer onboarding guides with Day 1, Week 1, and Month 1 sections.
Creates setup checklists for accounts, tools, repositories, and local development environments.
Outlines architecture, directory structure, workflows, and team processes for new engineers.
Builds first-task tutorials with milestones, review steps, and learning resources.
Adds FAQ and troubleshooting sections for common onboarding questions.
limitations: It needs accurate project details from the user to avoid generic or incorrect guidance.
It does not verify that commands, URLs, accounts, or team names are current.
Generated credential and access instructions require security review before publication.
It does not provision accounts, grant access, or enforce company policy.

use_cases.title: Prepare New Engineer Guides
use_cases.description: Create a complete onboarding guide before a developer joins the team.

use_cases.title: Document Project Setup
use_cases.description: Turn repository setup knowledge into a clear checklist for first-day development work.

use_cases.title: Improve Self-Service Onboarding
use_cases.description: Build FAQ, troubleshooting, and resource sections that reduce repeated team questions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Guide
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple onboarding document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a developer onboarding guide for a small web application team. Include Day 1 setup, key contacts, and first tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Customize for a Stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Create onboarding documentation for a React, Node.js, PostgreSQL, and Docker project. Include setup steps, architecture notes, and resources.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Learning Path
prompt_templates.scenario: Detailed request for staged learning goals.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a 30-day onboarding plan for a backend engineer. Include weekly goals, starter tickets, code review expectations, and checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Rewrite Existing Onboarding
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for improving current documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this onboarding outline and rewrite it into a complete guide. Flag missing access steps, unclear ownership, and risky credential instructions.

output_examples.input: A manager asks for onboarding material for a new full-stack developer.
output_examples.output: A structured guide with welcome notes, setup checklist, architecture overview, first feature task, team norms, and FAQ sections.

output_examples.input: A technical lead needs a first-week plan for a frontend hire.
output_examples.output: A five-day learning path with environment setup, component walkthroughs, testing expectations, buddy check-ins, and review milestones.

output_examples.input: A developer experience team wants to reduce repeated setup questions.
output_examples.output: A self-service onboarding document with troubleshooting, common gotchas, links to maintained resources, and clear ownership for help requests.

best_practices: Provide project-specific facts, owners, and maintained links before generating final onboarding content.
Review setup commands and credential guidance with security and platform owners.
Update the guide after each onboarding cycle using feedback from new hires.
anti_patterns: Publishing generated commands without testing them in a clean environment.
Including real secrets, shared passwords, or private URLs in onboarding examples.
Treating onboarding as a single document without checkpoints, ownership, or updates.

faq.question: Can this skill create a complete onboarding guide?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft a structured guide with setup, learning goals, team process, resources, and FAQ sections.

faq.question: Does it inspect my repository automatically?
faq.answer: No. It relies on details provided by the user or files the assistant is asked to review.

faq.question: Can it write company-specific access steps?
faq.answer: Yes, if you provide the correct systems and owners. Remove any real secrets before sharing content.

faq.question: Is the generated setup guide ready to publish?
faq.answer: Not without review. Verify commands, URLs, contacts, access workflows, and security requirements first.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Who benefits most from this skill?
faq.answer: Engineering managers, technical leads, and developer experience teams preparing onboarding material for new developers.
